stem: P is the mother of Q. R is the father of Q. S is the father of R. T is the wife of S. U is the son of T but U is not R. V is the daughter of P. How is V related to U?

per_option_rationale.rationale: S and T are parents; their children are R and U (U is T's son but not R). R and P are parents of Q and V. U is R's sibling. V is R's daughter. So U is V's paternal uncle. Reversing the viewpoint, V is U's niece.
Treating U and V as being in the same generation (both children of R and P) by ignoring that U is T's son, not P's son, gives sister.
Reversing the view and stating the relation from V's perspective toward U (V's uncle) rather than from U's perspective gives aunt instead of niece.
Ignoring the clue that U is T's son (not R) and instead treating U as R's child puts U in V's generation, giving cousin.

explanation: Build the tree: S married T; their children are R and U. R married P; their children are Q and V. U is R's brother (sibling). V is R's daughter. U is therefore V's paternal uncle. From U's viewpoint, V is U's niece.

explanation_sections.punchline: 'U is T's son but not R' establishes U as R's sibling (same parents S and T), making U V's uncle and V U's niece.
explanation_sections.approach: Apply most-certain first: build the S-T family (children R and U). Build the R-P family (children Q and V). Cross-link: U is the sibling of R; V is the child of R. Sibling of parent = uncle. From U's side: child of sibling = niece. Confirm gender: V is female (daughter), so niece not nephew.
explanation_sections.lesson: In multi-generation trees, establish sibling links before computing cross-generation relations. The phrase 'X is Y's child but not Z' always signals a sibling of Z.
explanation_sections.timing: About 120 s. Two traps: (1) cousin by treating U as R's child; (2) aunt by reversing the direction of the uncle-niece relation.
